stat_summary: In 2019/20, 37% of women in England had used a public library service in the previous 12 months, compared with 26% of men, according to the Taking Part Survey. Overall, 34% of adults had used a library for any purpose, and 31% had done so in their own time or voluntarily.
stat_source_title: Libraries – Taking Part Survey 2019/20, Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport

male.headline: Overdue Recognition: 26 Per Cent of Men Still Use the Library, and They're Tired of Being Told They Don't Read
male.standfirst: New official figures confirm what every bloke already knows from the crime aisle: a quarter of British men still use the library, and they are getting precisely zero credit as readers.
male.image_caption: Ron, 58, in the stacks, minding his own business.
body_paragraphs: New official figures have confirmed what every bloke already knows from the crime aisle: men still use the library. Twenty-six per cent had done so in the previous year, and they receive, in return, precisely zero credit, usually because somebody has already decided they do not read.

“I went in for a crime thriller and came out with a book on the Romans and a fine from 2019,” said Ron, 58, from Stockport. “Nobody stamped my card with a medal. Nobody even lowered their voice to say well done.”

The same DCMS survey shows 34 per cent of adults used a library for any purpose, and that borrowing remains the main reason for going in. Campaigners are already calling for a Library Bloke Week, and for a reserved chair by the newspapers for men who are, in their words, “just having a look”.
Yet where is the outrage? Where is the documentary? Britain's quiet borrower slots the book back, alone, with only a faded ticket for company.
male.pull_quote: Nobody stamped my card with a medal. Nobody even lowered their voice to say well done.

female.headline: Keeping the Lights On: 37 Per Cent of Women Use the Library, and They're the Ones Bringing It Back on Time
female.standfirst: Official statistics have finally shown who is still propping up the public library, and it does not look anything like a casual browse.
female.image_caption: Janet, 49, with this week's reservations and last week's returns.
body_paragraphs: Official statistics have at last shown who is still propping up the public library. Thirty-seven per cent of women had used one in the previous year – 11 points more than men – which, to anyone who has ever stood at the issue desk with a child's reading record, will not come as a plot twist.

“He buys one airport paperback a year and calls himself a reader,” said Janet, 49, from Sheffield. “I had three reservations, a summer reading record and a printer queue, and nobody's named a quiet study room after me.”

Researchers note that 73 per cent of those who visit a library building do so to borrow, and that taking a child to an event is among the most common reasons for going in. Campaigners are demanding a Public Lending Act of Thanks and a national apology for the phrase “can you just return mine while you're there”.
Until then, the country's unofficial acquisitions department will keep the reservations list moving, one overdue picture book at a time.
female.pull_quote: I had three reservations, a summer reading record and a printer queue, and nobody's named a quiet study room after me.
